categories.name: It works
categories.notes: Build OK with 0 errors and 0 warnings. / returns 200 through the '/' domain on the Blog page and lists both posts as cards with an image, date, title and summary; the links work. Both posts render every block (rich text, image, rich text) with no fallback or exception text. All 7 images are the provided Unsplash photos, imported into a 'Blog' media folder and served through signed GetCropUrl URLs that load. Everything is published.

categories.name: Content modeling
categories.notes: Folders 8/8: heroBlock/richTextBlock/imageBlock are elements in Blocks, blogFrontPage/blogPost are documents in Pages. Block grid 6/7: both pages use one shared 'Page Blocks' grid with hero, rich text and image blocks and sensible properties, but imageBlock has no alt-text field (the caption 'Photo by … on Unsplash' doubles as alt), and the hero block is only used on the front page. Structure 5/5: siteRoot is the only root type and allows blogFrontPage, which allows only blogPost; templates are assigned; aliases are camelCase; 'Page Blocks' sits in Custom/Umbraco.BlockGrid. Hygiene 4/5: no compositions; publishDate, summary and heroImage are real properties; no orphans. But blogPost has a 'title' property that duplicates the node name.

categories.name: Code architecture & conventions
categories.notes: Both pages render through Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync, and the scaffold's blockgrid partials are untouched. There is one markup-free adapter per block at blockgrid/Components/<alias>.cshtml, and each maps BlockGridItem<T> to a plain record in Models/Blog/ and calls Component.InvokeAsync. Hero, RichText and Image ViewComponents render Shared/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml with no Umbraco dependency. The post listing is a page-level PostList ViewComponent fed plain PostCardModels built with Children<BlogPost>(), Url() and GetCropUrl. Program.cs and appsettings.json are untouched, and there are no migrations. Tailwind was built into wwwroot/dist/site.css. _ViewImports.cshtml was only rewritten with different line endings.

categories.name: Content & presentation
categories.notes: Content 4/6: both posts are on-topic and accurate (one contract instead of bespoke adapters, typed tool schemas, client-agnostic servers, an auditable interface, read-back feedback loops), use 3 blocks each, and have fitting photos with correct photographer credits. They are thin, though: about 4 short paragraphs (~150 words) per post, closer to a teaser than a substantive article. Presentation 4/4: clean Tailwind layout, a hero banner, a two-card listing with images, dates and excerpts, readable post pages with a full-width header image, a captioned inline image and a back link.

categories.name: Process & honesty
categories.notes: Schema and content were built entirely over MCP (43 calls), with no browser, migration, Management API, uSync or DB use. The order of operations was right: model, then content, then stop/build/restart, then Razor. The run stayed in the project folder and did no memory access, and metrics.json has no warnings. The final report is accurate: it discloses the missing credits on the hero photos, that it didn't check visually, that it didn't verify uSync export, and the overlapping-build slip.

summary: A clean, fully working MCP-built blog: a front page with a hero and card listing, plus two posts built from a shared hero/rich-text/image block grid. The rendering pipeline follows the scaffold's conventions exactly. The main weakness is that the two posts are short (about 4 brief paragraphs each).
strengths: All 43 automated checks pass; build has 0 warnings
Textbook block pipeline: GetBlockGridHtmlAsync → markup-free adapters → ViewComponents with plain records
Correct folders, allowed children, templates, domain and media folder, all via MCP
Provided Unsplash photos imported and served with GetCropUrl; captions credit the right photographers
Polished Tailwind presentation; honest final report
